item.title: Michigan church shooting: 4 killed, several injured as gunman opens fire on worshippers
item.description: A Michigan church service turned horrific when a gunman crashed his truck, opened fire, and set the building ablaze, killing two and injuring eight. Police shot dead the attacker, Thomas Jacob Sanford, a 40-year-old former US Marine. The 10-minute rampage left the church destroyed, with authorities investigating the motive behind this shocking act of violence.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Denmark claims drone sightings, Nato vigilance up
item.description: Denmark's defence ministry reported new drone sightings at military sites overnight, raising security concerns in northern Europe amid suspected Russian aggression. This follows NATO's increased vigilance in the Baltic Sea region. Consequently, Denmark will ban civilian drone flights from Monday to Friday during an upcoming EU summit in Copenhagen.

item.title: Trump to meet Congress leaders to avert shutdown
item.description: Congressional leaders and President Trump meet Monday to avert a government shutdown, with federal funding expiring Tuesday. Democrats demand health-care provisions in the short-term spending bill, which Republicans want to pass first. The House-approved bill needs seven Democratic Senate votes, as Trump threatens federal worker firings.

item.title: Lost contact with 2 hostages: Hamas; 77 killed in 24 hrs, says Gaza ministry
item.description: Hamas's military wing announced losing contact with two Israeli hostages in Gaza City, urging Israel to withdraw troops and halt airstrikes for 24 hours to facilitate their retrieval. This development, with significant Israeli domestic resonance, could overshadow an upcoming meeting between Netanyahu and Trump, as Israel continued its advances despite the plea.

item.title: Moldovans vote in a tense election amid claims of Russian interference
item.description: Moldovans cast ballots in a tense parliamentary election Sunday, facing a pivotal choice between European Union integration and a drift back towards Moscow, amidst claims of Russian interference. The governing pro-Western party risks losing its majority to Russia-friendly opponents, creating significant uncertainty about the country's future geopolitical course. Separately, Telegram's founder accused French intelligence of seeking censorship of Moldovan channels.

item.title: UN arms embargo, other sanctions reimposed on Iran over its N-plans
item.description: The UN has reinstated an arms embargo and other sanctions on Iran over its nuclear program, triggered by European powers due to alleged violations of the 2015 deal. This move, which Iran denies, has been hailed by Israel and caused the Iranian rial to plummet. The sanctions include bans on uranium enrichment and ballistic missile activities.

item.title: Nepal probe panel recommends seizing passports of Oli and 4 others
item.description: A judicial commission investigating the suppression of Nepal's Gen Z protests recommended seizing the passports of deposed PM KP Sharma Oli and four others. They must now seek permission to leave Kathmandu, ensuring accountability as investigations proceed. This follows Oli's denial of shooting orders during the protests, which resulted in 75 deaths and his ouster.

item.title: Former Chinese agriculture minister is sentenced to death for graft
item.description: China's former agriculture minister, Tang Renjian, was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for accepting $38 million in bribes between 2007 and 2024. His political rights are revoked, and all personal property confiscated. This sentencing underscores Beijing's extensive anti-corruption campaign, which has disciplined over a million officials since 2012.

item.title: Mansi Kasliwal becomes 1st woman to head Caltech's Palomar Observatory
item.description: Professor Mansi Manoj Kasliwal has been appointed director of Palomar Observatory, making her the first woman and second PIO to lead the facility. An internationally recognized Caltech astronomer, she is celebrated for pioneering work on explosive cosmic events and transient astronomy, including multi-messenger observations. Kasliwal also mentors researchers and champions diversity in astrophysics.
item.dc:creator: Chethan Kumar

item.title: World's highest bridge opens to traffic in China
item.description: China inaugurated the world's highest bridge, the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge, towering 2,051 feet above a river in Guizhou province. Concurrently, Polish skier Andrzej Bargiel achieved a historic first by climbing and skiing down Mount Everest without supplemental oxygen, a remarkable feat given the extreme conditions at high altitude.

item.title: 'Best Oval Office ever': Donald Trump hails 24-Karat gold revamp; boasts foreign leaders 'freak out' by its grandeur
item.description: Donald Trump praised the 24-karat gold in the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, calling it the "best ever" and noting foreign leaders' awe. He personally purchased and expanded the gold decor, adding trim, cherubim, and trophies. His "gold guy" replicated Mar-a-Lago's gilded style, leading to a "golden office for the golden age."
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who was Thomas Jacob Sanford? US marine veteran who opened fire at Michigan church
item.description: US Marine veteran Thomas Jacob Sanford drove his Chevy Silverado into a Michigan Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints before opening fire. Sanford, who served in Iraq, was a family man with a young son. This incident occurred hours after the church's president, Russell M Nelson, passed away.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Bibi wants the deal too’: Donald Trump says Gaza plan well-received; cites all parties ‘tired of war’
item.description: US President Donald Trump voiced optimism for his 21-point Gaza peace plan, citing a "very good response" and anticipating Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu's support. The UN-unveiled proposal includes hostage returns and renewed dialogue for coexistence. Trump and Netanyahu are set to meet Monday to finalize the deal, aiming for a new regional future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘List of words to avoid’: US energy department bans use of ‘climate change’, ‘green’ in official communications; cites administrative priorities
item.description: The US Energy Department's EERE has controversially banned key terms like “climate change,” “green,” and “emissions” from its communications, aligning with the current administration's views. This directive follows President Trump's dismissal of global warming as a “hoax” and Energy Secretary Chris Wright's cancellation of renewable energy funding, signaling a significant shift in US energy policy and climate discourse.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Remarkable life’: Donald Trump pays tribute to LDS church president Russell M Nelson
item.description: Russell M. Nelson, President and Prophet of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, died at 101. Donald Trump paid tribute to the former heart surgeon and spiritual leader. Nelson implemented significant changes during his tenure, including discontinuing the term "Mormon" and overseeing increased temple construction worldwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: Dubai Police adds three new luxury Mercedes-Benz patrol cars to their supercar fleet
item.description: On World Tourism Day, Dubai Police expanded its luxury patrol fleet with three new Mercedes-Benz vehicles—the SL 55 AMG, GT 63 AMG, and electric EQS 580. Equipped with advanced AI and sustainable technologies, these cars enhance safety and service at key tourist spots. The addition underscores the strong partnership between Dubai Police and Mercedes-Benz in promoting modern, community-focused policing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mayoral shake-up: NYC mayor Eric Adams ends reelection bid; clears way for three-way race
item.description: New York City Mayor Eric Adams has ended his reelection bid, setting up a three-way race for the city's top office between Zohran Mamdani, Andrew Cuomo, and Curtis Sliwa. Adams' withdrawal, announced via video, comes amidst low poll numbers and a corruption scandal, though his name will still appear on the November ballot. This significantly alters the mayoral contest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Will be expanded’: Netanyahu says Gaza strikes will not threaten Abraham Accords; addresses Trump’s 21-point Gaza peace plan
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, ahead of meeting Donald Trump, affirmed that the Gaza conflict and recent strikes would not imperil the Abraham Accords, expecting their expansion. He discussed Trump's 21-point Gaza peace plan, aiming to dismantle Hamas and establish new governance, while rejecting Palestinian Authority control due to reform doubts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Nigel Max Edge? Suspect identified and charged in North Carolina shooting; once accompanied ‘American Idol’ star to event
item.description: Nigel Max Edge, 40, faces three murder and five attempted murder charges after opening fire from a boat at a Southport, NC restaurant, killing three and wounding five. The combat veteran, reportedly suffering from PTSD, previously escorted Kellie Pickler to the CMAs and claimed friendly fire in Iraq by "LGBTQ White Supremacists."
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Unwanted, unneeded, un-American’: Portland leaders slam Trump’s threatened troop deployment; issue open letter
item.description: Portland leaders, including the Metro Chamber, Governor Kotek, and Senators, issued an open letter opposing President Trump's plan to deploy federal troops. They warn the "unwanted" intervention would undermine the city's recovery, damage its reputation, and disrupt progress in reducing violence, recalling the negative impact of the 2020 deployment.
